answer: One-chip identity binding requires each agent identity to present a distinct physical unclonable chip whose crystal oscillator timing contributes to a fresh challenge-response. The registry records each chip’s signed response in an append-only ledger, replacing the old quill log, and rejects any chip reused by a second active identity. A gale of registrations from one operator still pays a chip plus physical intake inspection and shipping per identity; cloning is blocked because the chip’s secret cannot be copied.
